name: Commission v Bulgaria (C-488/15) (PM10)

jurisdiction.court: Court of Justice of the European Union (CJEU) – Third Chamber

description: Infringement proceedings against Bulgaria for the systematic and continuous exceedance of the daily and annual limit values for PM10 (Directive 2008/50/EC) in numerous zones and agglomerations, from 2007 to 2014, and for the failure to adopt appropriate measures under Article 23. The CJEU's first major litigation on air quality.
outcome: Action upheld. The CJEU ruled against Bulgaria for infringement of Articles 13 and 23 of Directive 2008/50/EC, laying down the principle that the exceedance of the limit values is in itself sufficient to constitute a failure to fulfil obligations and that it is for the State to demonstrate, by means of credible plans, a return to compliance in the shortest possible time. Direct precedent for the subsequent case law against Poland, Italy, France.
